column3: Native account commands plus a three-stream WebSocket mux (account/watch, account/watchExpiry, productAnalytics/watchPolicy); accountView() re-projects the wire state through a closed whitelist and validateBrowserDestination() allows only HTTPS or HTTP-on-loopback URLs with no embedded credentials.

Owns one backend startup/teardown independent of windows: an Attempt generation token makes a late child failure from a replaced attempt a no-op, stop() cancels an attempt mid-prepare and mid-start, and a startup failure plus a cleanup failure merge into an AggregateError.

One-time Windows confirmation before hiding to the tray; the acknowledgement is a marker file under Electron userData (survives updates, removed on uninstall) and repeated close requests focus the open prompt instead of stacking one.

Per-workspace partition and per-tab lease for sidebar webview guests; will-attach-webview deletes every renderer-supplied preference except disablePopups and assigns a fixed isolation policy, and the guest session denies all permissions, downloads and any request to the app's own Host.

Desktop client identity for Platform calls: desktopClientVersion() throws when DSH_CLIENT_VERSION is absent rather than reporting a guess, and timezoneOffsetSeconds converts getTimezoneOffset's minutes-west into seconds-east.
Two-line ambient declaration (declare module '*.css') so the standalone Welcome renderer can import the shared design-platform and gradient-shadow-text stylesheets.

Mounts the Welcome React renderer with flushSync so the first paint is complete before Electron shows the window, and mirrors prefers-color-scheme onto a body data-ds-dark-theme attribute, cleaning up the matchMedia listener and the root on pagehide.

The standalone welcome flow (sign in / API key / skip); a revision counter is a stale-response guard on every async action, busyRef gates double submits synchronously, and the API-key validator rejects quotes, whitespace and NAME=value prefixes.

Reversible dsh CLI link ownership: the observed state is fingerprinted over lstat fields plus the symlink target, the old entry is renamed aside and re-verified (ESTALE on mismatch), and every failure path restores it and names the preserved path.

Native Manage-dsh-Command dialog; the mutation runs in a separate worker with KEY/SECRET/TOKEN/PASSWORD/NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_PATH stripped from the environment, macOS escalates via osascript only for mutations, and shellCommand() probes command -v dsh to detect a shadowing install.

Private worker entry: the mutation destination is a constant in the worker (/usr/local/bin/dsh) so elevation cannot be steered, macOS uses umask 022 because it writes public metadata, and Windows pipes JSON on stdin to a bundled command-path.ps1.

Validates the signed local npm tarball set: name/version/file/integrity regexes, mandatory sorted-by-name ordering, a directory listing that must match the descriptor exactly, sha512 re-hashing, and a lockfile scan that refuses any registry resolution of a packaged core name.

Crash report files: a bounded renderer-console tail (head-trimmed, one oversized line kept whole), util.inspect with depth 6 and a 256 KiB cut, a strict file-name regex so pruning touches only its own reports, and 10 reports retained.

Machine description for the feedback questionnaire (platform, os, app_arch, cpu, memory_gib); each field is collected independently and omitted when its source throws, and no hostname or user name is included.

Window-owned directory dialog: the sender and main frame are checked, an in-flight pick is stored in a WeakMap and reused so a second request joins the first, and the window is restored and focused before the native dialog opens.
Shared duration validator: an environment duration must be an integer from 1000 through 2147483647 (setTimeout's own range) and an invalid value throws naming the variable rather than being clamped.

First-fatal-failure recovery: the crash report is written first and bounded to 1 s so the dialog can name it, the detail is budgeted to 1200 characters keeping the last 8 lines, an EADDRINUSE match swaps in a specific message, and a failed recovery operation re-prompts.

Owns the child Host process: a hand-written validator (isDesktopHostEvent) checks every IPC message before it is trusted and kills the child on a malformed one, stderr is a bounded 64 KiB tail, stop() escalates SIGTERM to SIGKILL over three deadlines, and requireGraceful refuses the update unless the child acknowledged the shutdown and exited 0.
Four-line file holding DESKTOP_HOST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 4, the compile-time constant that parseDesktopRelease compares against so the shell and the Host cannot disagree about the lifecycle protocol.

Typed preload contract: the DESKTOP_IPC channel names, the DesktopUpdateState/Presentation split (renderers get a semantic status and never a version, URL or installation authorization), and assertDesktopSender which checks the frame's protocol and hostname against an allowlist.

Binds the shared ShortcutPersistence to Electron userData (keybindings.json, written atomically at mode 0600) and publishes the snapshot after commit; a missing file is a normal first-run path, not an error.

Native key dispatch: physical keys are intercepted, chords (two-key pairs) are matched on desktop platforms, the close-page accelerator is separated from user bindings, and an editingInput bypass lets the native Edit menu send keys to the focused editor; the preload re-verifies the target frame for iframe and webview input.

English and Chinese shell copy: DesktopMessages is a mapped type over every English key and zh satisfies it, so a missing translation is a compile error; formatDesktopMessage leaves an unknown placeholder visible rather than rendering undefined.

Reads the POSIX login-shell environment once (the account record's shell, not $SHELL, then fixed shells) using a NUL-delimited env dump; the read completes at the closing delimiter because rc-started children can hold stdout open, and DSH_*/ELECTRON_* and probe-session variables are never merged.

The Electron entry point: single-instance ownership, window creation, the dsh-app protocol handler (shell documents served locally, /app/* forwarded to the Host with its cookie), the boot/quit lifecycle, and the ordered update-install handoff (task lock, Platform cleanup, clean stop, then quit).
Four-line dependency-free channel-name module (status, state, action) so the sandboxed mandatory-update preload does not have to import the main-process graph.

Server-driven mandatory-update policy: a known block survives transport and parsing failures but not a fresh no-force success, concurrent checks share one request, the backoff is exponential with jitter, and the policy-supplied page URL is re-validated against the deployment allowlist immediately before use.

Shell-owned modal policy UI: install and later require a live confirmation revision (a stale prompt is refused), the Windows build embeds the block in the main window and re-blocks on reload, closing the blocked window quits the app, and a copy action reads the clipboard back to confirm the address was retained.
Microphone access is granted only to the primary application's main frame on the dsh-app://app origin for audio only, and on macOS only when the OS has already granted microphone access.

Builds the Node-mode child environment: ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 plus a prepended bundled node shim directory and DSH_DESKTOP_NODE_EXECUTABLE, so one shipped executable serves as both shell and runtime.
Hand-rolled recursive removal of an owned directory that unlinks symlinks instead of following them, because Electron's recursive rm follows nested Windows junctions into installed resources.
Resolves the two Electron-owned paths under the shared Harness home (profiles/desktop and profiles/desktop/lock), so the desktop profile and the npm-installed dsh share one home.
Channel names and the Platform locale type for the Platform bridge; the Platform vocabulary is en_US/zh_CN while the desktop one is en/zh-CN, and the translation happens in the main process.

Isolated Platform documents: an account-scoped persistent partition (hashed from origin and user id) or a random temporary one, header injection restricted to the account origin with injected names stripped from redirected subresources, and storage sanitized before the view loads so an unclean exit cannot leave a stale session.

Isolated Feishu login for the policy: the same class both presents the window and performs the authenticated request, which is restricted to one exact endpoint with credentials include and redirect error; a local placeholder paints first so the remote page is not a blank window.

The product preload: every exposed surface is gated on the dsh-app://app origin and the main frame, the keyboard subscriber re-verifies the target iframe or webview in the renderer, and webUtils.getPathForFile turns a dropped file into a path reference instead of an upload.

Lease-scoped browser bridge exposing acquire/release/onOpenRequested and no IPC or Electron objects; one main-process subscription per window is demultiplexed to per-lease listener sets, and a failing listener cannot stop the others.

Embeds the shell's mandatory-update document in the Windows main window with a closed shadow root and a private MessageChannel (not the shared ipcRenderer), covering the content area but not the native caption, and blocking background keys while the block is active.
Isolated bridge for the mandatory-update modal, exposed only when location.href is exactly dsh-app://shell/mandatory-update.html; the main process independently re-checks the sender frame and URL.

Windows caption menubar in a shadow root, whose open action restores the editor's focus and selection (including selectionStart/End and cloned Ranges) so a native menu does not steal the caret; the mount waits for the AppFrame's data-shell-overlay seat.

Copies the Platform token and locale once via a synchronous bootstrap and caches them in closure variables, exposing them only when the page origin equals the origin the main process named; a failed bootstrap leaves embedded mode rather than falling back to browser credentials.
Marks html[data-platform] and mirrors the fullscreen state onto html[data-fullscreen] so shared Web CSS can scope desktop-only rules, handling the preload running before the document root exists.

Mirrors html[data-ds-theme-source] into Electron's nativeTheme.themeSource via a MutationObserver, deduplicating on the last sent value, so native chrome, macOS vibrancy and the Platform login palette follow the app's theme rather than the OS.
Response-only bridge for the shell update dialog, exposed only at the exact update-dialog.html URL; the document may answer with a revision and a displayed index and can name no version or URL.

Delivers the localized welcome copy through the preload (resolved from a --dsh-welcome-locale argument, whose absence throws) and exposes only write-only credential actions and safe account snapshots; analytics is gated on a second IPC so the policy is checked per event.

Measures the renderer's actual palette (hidden probe span painted into a 1x1 canvas) and sends the rgba values for the native title-bar overlay, re-measuring on lang, theme-attribute and head changes so a custom theme keeps native chrome in sync.

Profile preparation under a pid lock file (regular-file check, stale-lock reclamation via process.kill(owner,0) and ESRCH), a pnpm workspace with an explicit allowBuilds allowlist, and a legacy pnpm-workspace.yaml migration that only rewrites an exact legacy text.

Quit confirmation driven by a bounded Host inspection: an unknown inspection result warns about running tasks rather than quitting silently, the inspection runs once per decision, and the button array is the same but macOS lays it out right-to-left (Quit right of Cancel) while Windows keeps array order.

Immutable release identity (version, hostProtocolVersion, nodeVersion, pnpmVersion) validated with semver; the host protocol version must equal the compile-time constant, so the shell and its bundled Host cannot disagree.

Integrity record for the shipped runtime tree: every file is hashed and sized into desktop-runtime.json, paths are validated against traversal, links are never followed, and verification re-inventories with up to 8 concurrent readers and strips the executable bit on Windows before comparing.

Shell settings read once per process from userData/desktop/settings.json: the default file is created only when missing (wx, 0600) and any read, parse or validation failure falls back to defaults with a warning instead of blocking startup.
Claims the Electron single-instance lock at module scope, before whenReady, so a losing process never touches the profile; a later launch focuses the owner through the second-instance event.
Flattens an Error or AggregateError into a serializable message for a renderer, expanding the AggregateError's sub-messages so a nested cleanup failure is visible rather than hidden.

Windows tray present for the whole run (not only while the window is hidden), relabelled in the current locale, whose Quit goes through the same confirmation as every other quit entry; creation failure only warns.

Best-effort background attention for a prepared update: one reminder per downloaded version, cleared the moment either window takes focus, using taskbar flash or a dock bounce plus a silent notification that returns to the confirmation without installing.
Reads the installer-sealed update channel from the packaged manifest: an absent key means nightly but an invalid explicit value throws so a typo cannot silently switch the feed.

Version-bound update flow with autoDownload and autoInstallOnAppQuit off, allowDowngrade off and prereleases allowed only on nightly; download and install both re-check the exact confirmed version, and dispose awaits pending operations before detaching the error listener so shutdown cannot emit an unhandled error.

Main-owned update confirmation: every prompt carries a revision and a stale response is rejected, the document may answer only with a displayed index, prompts can be replaced in place, and an AbortSignal lets the mandatory policy cancel all ordinary dialogs at once.

Twelve-line separation of three concerns in the update preparation error: a stable kind shared by the native and Web presentations, locale-owned recovery copy, and optional main-owned technical details that exclude subprocess output and credentials.

Electron-native INACTIVITY deadline for the updater transport: the timer is refreshed on every response chunk (a large but progressing download is never killed), the upstream Node socket timer is unusable so the refresh loop is re-implemented, and the Electron 44 close-before-headers quirk is handled.

Opt-in JSONL update evidence outside the installation directory: a whitelist keeps only phase, target version, integer percent, failed operation and one of eight fixed error codes, duplicate states are dropped, and a failed append propagates so incomplete qualification is never reported as traced.

Shell-owned modal overlays as child windows that follow the parent's bounds and survive a renderer reload; a per-parent counter plus a revision publishes the blocked state to the keyboard layer, and on macOS the parent's input blocker is prepended so it runs before the product's shortcut listeners.

Classifies an update failure into nine stable kinds (a network regex produces the -network variants) and derives the localized summary from the kind, so the native dialog and the Web status indicator cannot disagree; the renderer-facing presentation carries no raw diagnostics.

Update polling with a completion-based deadline (the next check is scheduled when the previous finishes), exponential backoff on failure with symmetric jitter, a monotonic performance.now clock, and an activeChecks counter so joined manual callers advance the delay only once.

Serves the local Web document and forwards /app/* to the Host with its cookie: the index is rewritten to inject a __DSH_BOOT_READY__ promise, paths are checked against the root (403 on traversal), set-cookie and hop-by-hop headers are withheld, and plugin bundle responses are forced to no-store because the Host's revision changes every launch.

The welcome renderer's contract: nine private channels, a closed analytics event vocabulary, needsWelcome() which is true only when neither an account login nor an API key is configured, and a save result that carries no Host diagnostics.

Native welcome operations over the shared Web RPC: every call carries a fresh rpcId that the response must match, credential references are read in batches of 64 because describe accepts at most 64, and a key save failure is swallowed into {ok:false} because provider diagnostics may contain credentials.

Opens the sole native welcome window with a locale-only preload argument; the WELCOME_IPC handlers are removed and re-installed on every window so two windows can never both answer, the analytics handler validates the event name and attribute shape, and the window is shown only after the document loads.
One constant (WINDOWS_TITLEBAR_HEIGHT = 40) shared by the native titleBarOverlay, the CSS variable and the mandatory-overlay offset, so the caption, the clearance and the overlay cannot drift apart.
